summary: Target-level plan of H4 and H5. H4: set-level radial loci (closed disc, punctured disc, closed annulus, strict locus, and the analytic open disc and annulus as unions, which differ from strict loci at rank-two points); Berkovich's classification of tame coverings of discs and annuli; the Kummer generator and the prime-to-residue cohomology, proper-support cohomology and restriction maps of discs, punctured discs and annuli, over Spa(C, O_C) and, for ordinary cohomology, over arbitrary plus rings; the root-extraction tower of ECD 19.5; Huber's constructibility of R f_! for smooth morphisms in Ito's form, and its transfer to strictly totally disconnected bases. H5: Huber's comparison theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1 (identifiers of the reviewed decomposition kept), finiteness for smooth spaces, the ball system and radius argument of ECD 27.2, and Lütkebohmert's local compactification of smooth rigid curves with the boundary reduction of ECD's biduality proof. Geometry and general sheaf theory are imported from their owners under the accepted RS-05. Open inputs are recorded: Huber's book proofs, relative duality in every dimension (RT-AREA-etale/5), the characteristic-zero route of 3.8.1, and Lütkebohmert's theorem over a nondiscretely valued field.

nodes.title: The closed-disc radial locus
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A with a topology, a subring A⁺, a coordinate T ∈ A and a radius representative b ∈ A, closedDisc(A⁺,T,b) is the set of points v of the pinned Spa(A,A⁺) (continuous valuations with v ≤ 1 on A⁺) such that T ≤ᵥ b. For a unit b it is the pinned rational subset R({T}/b), hence relatively open in Spa(A,A⁺), and it is unchanged when T and b are multiplied by the same unit. For A = C⟨T⟩ over a complete nontrivially valued field C and b = ϖ_b ∈ C^× it is the underlying set of the closed disc of radius |ϖ_b| (Ito's B(ε), Berkovich's E(0,r) on rank-one points), an affinoid open subspace supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A2. The valuative comparison is taken at every rank: a weak inequality gives an open subset of the adic space, whereas a strict inequality gives a closed constructible subset (Ito, p. 37), so the words closed and open of radial terminology are not adic-topological.
hypotheses: A commutative ring with a topology and an explicit plus subring A⁺ for the set-level construction (the pinned spa asks for nothing more); sheafiness, completeness and the Huber hypotheses belong to AdicSpacesPartII R0.
For analytic discs and annuli: C complete nontrivially valued, radius representatives a, b ∈ C^× with |a| ≤ |b|.
proofSteps: Intersect the pinned set spa(A⁺) with {v | T ≤ᵥ b}.

For a unit b the denominator condition of the pinned rational subset holds at every valuation (b ≤ᵥ 0 would give 1 = b·b⁻¹ ≤ᵥ 0), so mem_rationalSubset_iff gives closedDisc(A⁺,T,b) = rationalSubset(A⁺,{T},b). Relative openness is then isOpen_val_preimage_rationalSubset, and invariance under (T,b) ↦ (Tu,bu) for a unit u is rationalSubset_image_mul_right.

Base change: for a continuous φ: A → B with φ(A⁺) ⊆ B⁺, comap_mem_spa puts comap φ v in spa(A⁺) for v ∈ spa(B⁺), and comap_vle turns T ≤ b at comap φ v into φ(T) ≤ φ(b) at v; for a unit b this is comap_preimage_rationalSubset_inter_spa with numerator set {T}.

Monotonicity in the radius is transitivity of ≤ᵥ. The affinoid ring, the structure sheaf and the open immersion of the analytic disc are AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc (rescaled); nothing but a set is constructed here.

nodes.title: The punctured-disc radial locus
nodes.statement: puncturedDisc(A⁺,T,b) is closedDisc(A⁺,T,b) minus the support locus of T, that is the set of v ∈ Spa(A,A⁺) with T ≤ᵥ b and not T ≤ᵥ 0. For the unit disc over a complete nontrivially valued field it is Ito's B(ε)^* = B(ε)∖{0}: the complement of the classical point T = 0, an open subspace of the disc. It is not the complement of a reduction fibre or of a residue disc.
hypotheses: A commutative ring with a topology and an explicit plus subring A⁺ for the set-level construction (the pinned spa asks for nothing more); sheafiness, completeness and the Huber hypotheses belong to AdicSpacesPartII R0.
For analytic discs and annuli: C complete nontrivially valued, radius representatives a, b ∈ C^× with |a| ≤ |b|.
proofSteps: Intersect closedDisc(A⁺,T,b) with the complement of {v | T ≤ᵥ 0}.
puncturedDisc(A⁺,0,b) = ∅ because 0 ≤ᵥ 0, and puncturedDisc(A⁺,1,1) = Spa(A,A⁺) because 1 ≤ᵥ 0 fails at every valuation.
Over a field C the support locus of T in Spa(C⟨T⟩) is the single classical point 0, which is closed; the open subspace structure of its complement is A2's.

nodes.title: The closed-annulus radial locus
nodes.statement: closedAnnulus(A⁺,T,a,b) is the set of v ∈ Spa(A,A⁺) with a ≤ᵥ T ≤ᵥ b and T outside the support of v. For all a, b it equals R({T}/b) ∩ R({a}/T) for the pinned rational subsets: no unit hypothesis is needed, because T outside the support and T ≤ᵥ b put b outside the support. Over a complete nontrivially valued field C, with a = ϖ_a, b = ϖ_b ∈ C^× and |ϖ_a| ≤ |ϖ_b|, it is the affinoid annulus with coordinate ring C⟨T, ϖ_a/T, T/ϖ_b⟩ (Ito's B(a,b), Berkovich's A(r,R) on rank-one points); equal radii give the circle and are allowed. Ito calls B(a,b) an open annulus because it is an open subspace; the name closedAnnulus follows the classical convention r ≤ |T| ≤ R.
hypotheses: A commutative ring with a topology and an explicit plus subring A⁺ for the set-level construction (the pinned spa asks for nothing more); sheafiness, completeness and the Huber hypotheses belong to AdicSpacesPartII R0.
For analytic discs and annuli: C complete nontrivially valued, radius representatives a, b ∈ C^× with |a| ≤ |b|.
proofSteps: Intersect spa(A⁺) with {a ≤ᵥ T}, {T ≤ᵥ b} and the complement of the support of T.

By mem_rationalSubset_iff, R({T}/b) ∩ R({a}/T) is cut out by T ≤ᵥ b, b outside the support, a ≤ᵥ T and T outside the support; the second condition follows from the first and the fourth by transitivity.
closedAnnulus(A⁺,0,a,b) = ∅ and closedAnnulus(A⁺,1,1,1) = Spa(A,A⁺); monotonicity in both radii is transitivity of ≤ᵥ.

Annular exhaustion of the punctured disc: if ϖ is topologically nilpotent and v is continuous with T outside its support, the set {x | v(x) < v(T)} is an open neighbourhood of 0 and contains ϖⁿ for large n, so puncturedDisc(A⁺,T,b) = ⋃ₙ closedAnnulus(A⁺,T,ϖⁿ,b) (compare Ito, p. 38: D(1)∖{0} = ⋃_ε D(1) ∩ B(ε,1)).
The affinoid presentation and the open immersion into the disc are A2's.

nodes.title: The strict-valuative annulus locus
nodes.statement: strictAnnulus(A⁺,T,a,b) imposes a<ᵥT<ᵥb and T outside support on Spa(A,A⁺); strict means the negation of the reverse weak comparison, as in Mathlib ValuativeRel.vlt. It is the locus with strict bounds at every rank. A strict-valuative locus is not asserted to be an open subset of the adic topology: topology and the corresponding pseudo-adic/support convention are supplied by A2/H0. In geometric Berkovich or rigid terminology the associated region is called an open annulus; the words open and closed in radial terminology do not determine adic topological openness.
hypotheses: A commutative ring with a topology and an explicit plus subring A⁺ for the set-level construction (the pinned spa asks for nothing more); sheafiness, completeness and the Huber hypotheses belong to AdicSpacesPartII R0.
For analytic discs and annuli: C complete nontrivially valued, radius representatives a, b ∈ C^× with |a| ≤ |b|.
No openness is asserted for the strict locus.
proofSteps: Intersect spa(A⁺) with {a <ᵥ T}, {T <ᵥ b} and the complement of the support of T, where x <ᵥ y is the negation of y ≤ᵥ x (Mathlib's ValuativeRel.vlt).
A strict comparison implies the weak one by totality of ≤ᵥ, so strictAnnulus ⊆ closedAnnulus; a <ᵥ T and T <ᵥ a are contradictory, so strictAnnulus(A⁺,T,a,a) = ∅.

Over a field the strict locus is not open: Ito's D(ε) = {|T| < ε} is a closed constructible subset of B(1), and the rank-two point η(b) of Example A.1 has |T| infinitesimally smaller than b, so it lies in the strict locus while its rank-one generalisation, the Gauss point of radius b, does not. The pseudo-adic support convention for such loci is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site.

Berkovich's open annulus B(r′, r) is the complement of a closed disc in an open disc; on rank-one points it is the strict locus r′ < |T − a| < r.

acceptance: Equal radii give the empty set; a valuation with T equivalent to an endpoint is excluded; a rank-two point infinitesimally inside the outer endpoint is included.

nodes.title: The analytic open-annulus exhaustion
nodes.statement: Given families of radius representatives a_j, b_j (j ∈ ℕ), openAnnulus(A⁺,T,a,b) = ⋃_j closedAnnulus(A⁺,T,a_j,b_j). Over a complete nontrivially valued field C, with 0 < r < |a_j| ≤ |b_j| < R, the |a_j| decreasing to r and the |b_j| increasing to R, the union is the analytic open annulus r < |T| < R: an open subspace of the disc, the union of an increasing chain of closed annuli (Ito, p. 38), and the adic space of Berkovich's B(r,R). It depends on the families only up to mutual cofinality. It is not the strict valuative locus {a <ᵥ T <ᵥ b} at the endpoints: by Ito's Example A.1 the rank-two points η(R) and η(r)′ satisfy the strict inequalities, their rank-one generalisations lie on the boundary circles, and they belong to no closed annulus of strictly smaller size, hence not to the union.

nodes.title: Tame covers of discs and annuli
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field with residue characteristic p ≥ 0. An étale morphism φ: Y → X of k-analytic curves is tame at y if the geometric ramification index v_φ(y) = [𝓗(y) : 𝓗(φ(y))] is not divisible by p, and tame if this holds at every point of Y; a Galois covering of degree prime to p is tame. Then every tame finite étale Galois covering of the closed disc E(0,r) is trivial, that is a disjoint union of copies of the disc (Berkovich, Theorem 6.3.2). Wild coverings exist in positive residue characteristic, so nothing is asserted without tameness. For radius in |k^×| the finite étale coverings of the Berkovich disc and of the adic disc are given by the same finite étale algebras over the affinoid ring, and tameness is tested at rank-one points, so the statement holds for the adic closed disc over Spa(k, k°).
hypotheses: k algebraically closed and complete; the valuation may be trivial in Berkovich's statement, and is nontrivial with radius in |k^×| for the adic form.
Tame means: the geometric ramification index is prime to the residue characteristic at every point, not merely that the degree is invertible in k.
proofSteps: Berkovich's proof of 6.3.2: for a connected covering of degree n > 1 the set Σ of points of E(0,r) with fewer than n preimages is closed; points of types (1) and (4) are not in Σ because 𝓗(x) = k there has divisible value group, and the analysis of the remaining points produces a nontrivial finite étale Galois covering of the affine line over the residue field of degree prime to p, which does not exist.
Remark 6.3.1 (ii): the geometric ramification index at y is the order of its stabiliser, so a Galois covering of degree prime to p is tame (Corollary 6.3.3).

Transport to the adic disc: finite étale coverings of a strictly affinoid space and of its adic space are the same finite étale algebras; the comparison of the two geometries is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/berkovich-taut-comparison.

Every tame finite étale Galois covering Y → A(r,R) with Y connected is standard, that is isomorphic to φ_n for n its degree (Berkovich, Theorem 6.3.5); a tame standard covering has n prime to p. The case r = R (a circle) is included. This classifies tame Galois coverings, not all finite étale coverings. For r, R ∈ |k^×| the same holds for the adic closed annulus over Spa(k, k°).

nodes.title: The annulus Kummer generator
nodes.statement: Let A be a closed annulus over Spa(C, O_C) with coordinate T and n ≥ 1 prime to the residue characteristic. annulusKummer(T) := δ_n(T) ∈ H¹(A, μ_n) is the image of the unit T under the Kummer connecting map of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/kummer-sequence. The map O(A)^×/n → H¹(A, μ_n) is an isomorphism, and the degree identifies both with ℤ/n so that δ_n(T) ↦ 1, where the degree of a unit c·T^m·(1 + h) (c ∈ C^×, sup|h| < 1) is m; on a boundary circle this is Berkovich's deg_D for the inner complementary disc D, the outer disc gives −m, and H3's residue map is γ_D = −deg_D. The identification is canonical for μ_n-coefficients and a coordinate; identifying H¹(A, ℤ/n) with ℤ/n needs a trivialisation of μ_n. The construction applies the imported connecting homomorphism; it does not define the Kummer sequence.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete, base Spa(C, O_C); the coordinate is a unit on A; n prime to the residue characteristic.
In the suggested file only the additive core (a homomorphism from the units to an abelian group) is typed, because the analytic site and δ_n are H0's.
proofSteps: Import δ_n and its naturality from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/kummer-sequence; since A is the adic spectrum of a principal ideal domain, Pic(A) = 0 and δ_n: O(A)^×/n → H¹(A, μ_n) is an isomorphism.

Every class in H¹(A, μ_n) is a μ_n-torsor, hence a tame Galois covering, which is standard (tame-annulus-covers); so H¹(A, μ_n) is generated by δ_n(T). Equivalently, units are c·T^m·(1 + h) with sup|h| < 1 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/local-residue-degree-formula (i) on a boundary circle), and c and 1 + h are n-th powers because C is algebraically closed and n is invertible in O_C.
δ_n is a homomorphism, so δ_n(S^e) = e·δ_n(S) and δ_n(T·uⁿ) = δ_n(T); constants have n-th roots in C.

nodes.title: Tame-root towers kill the annulus class
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a prime different from the residue characteristic p. (a) Let A′ → A be a morphism of closed annuli over a geometric base with coordinates S on A′ and T on A such that T pulls back to u·S^e with u an ℓ-th power of a unit. Then pullback H¹(A, μ_ℓ) → H¹(A′, μ_ℓ) sends δ_ℓ(T) to e·δ_ℓ(S): it is zero if ℓ | e and an isomorphism if ℓ ∤ e, in particular for p-power root extractions. (b) For a filtered system of such annuli in which ℓ-th roots of the coordinate are cofinally adjoined, colim H¹(−, F_ℓ) = 0 and colim H⁰(−, F_ℓ) = F_ℓ. (c) The ECD system: let k be an algebraically closed discrete field of characteristic p, (C′, C′⁺) a geometric field pair over k with pseudouniformiser ϖ, and for a finite extension L of k((t^{1/p^∞})) let Y′_{n,L} = {|t|ⁿ ≤ |ϖ| ≤ |t|^{1/n}} ⊂ Spa(L, O_L) ×_k Spa(C′, C′⁺). Each L is k((t_L^{1/p^∞})) for a uniformiser t_L of the corresponding finite separable extension of k((t)), each Y′_{n,L} is the perfection of a closed annulus over Spa(C′, C′⁺) in the coordinate t_L, and for L ⊂ L′ of ramification index e one has t_L = u·t_{L′}^e with u a unit of the integers of L′, hence an ℓ-th power. Therefore RΓ(lim_L Y′_{n,L}, F_ℓ) = F_ℓ: the classical input of ECD Theorem 19.5 (ii).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p; annuli over a geometric base Spa(C′, C′⁺), the plus ring of any rank (annulus-geometric-plus-ring).

Passage to the limit uses cohomological continuity for a colimit-presented tilde-limit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity), not an inverse limit of underlying spaces alone; the perfectoid annuli have the étale cohomology of the classical ones (perfection, part (v) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids).
proofSteps: (a) Naturality and additivity of the Kummer class (annulusKummer_natural, annulusKummer_pow) and vanishing on ℓ-th powers; δ_ℓ(S) generates H¹(A′, μ_ℓ) (annulus-kummer-generator).
(b) Every degree-one class dies at a later stage; degree-zero classes persist because the annuli are connected; higher degrees vanish at every stage.

(c) The units of the integers of L′ are c·(1 + m) with c ∈ k^× and m topologically nilpotent; both factors are ℓ-th powers since k is algebraically closed and ℓ is invertible. The cohomology of each stage is annulus-geometric-plus-ring; the limit is taken by tilde-limit continuity (ECD Proposition 14.9 in the source).

acceptance: An ℓ-th root transition is zero on H¹(−, F_ℓ); a p-th root transition is an isomorphism on H¹(−, F_ℓ), so a tower adjoining only p-power roots does not kill the class.

nodes.title: Constructibility of smooth proper-support direct images
nodes.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field with ring of integers O, Y an adic space over Spa(K, O) (locally the adic spectrum of a strongly noetherian Tate ring), f: X → Y a smooth, separated and quasi-compact morphism of adic spaces, n ≥ 1 invertible in O and F a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on X_ét. Then R^q f_!F is a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on Y for every q ≥ 0 (Hub96 Theorem 6.2.2, in the form of Ito's Theorem 6.8). In particular this holds for the relative closed unit ball B_Y → Y over every Y of topologically finite type over K, the case used in ECD Theorem 24.1. Constructible is Huber's notion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/classical-constructible-sheaves): a finite partition of every quasi-compact open into constructible locally closed subsets of all points, with locally constant restrictions of finite type; it is neither Zariski-constructibility nor finiteness of stalks. R^q f_!F vanishes for q > 2·dim f. The statement can fail for non-smooth f (Ito, Remark 6.9).
hypotheses: K algebraically closed, complete, nontrivially valued (the standing assumption of Ito's §6); Y in Huber's locally noetherian analytic scope; f smooth, separated, quasi-compact.
F constructible in Huber's sense; n ≥ 1 invertible in O.
The proof in Hub96 §6.2 was not read (the book is not public): the node is a source-backed leaf, recorded in the first gap.
proofSteps: Statement: Hub96 Theorem 6.2.2 as restated in Ito's Theorem 6.8; the book proof is not public and is not reproduced, so the node does not claim proof closure.

Relative ball: B_Y → Y is smooth, separated and quasi-compact (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc (d)), hence compactifiable, and R⁺f_! is that of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/proper-support-direct-image.

Vanishing above 2·dim f: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension. Compatibility with base change between locally noetherian bases: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/lower-shriek-base-change, which also identifies the stalks with compactly supported cohomology of geometric fibres.

nodes.title: Constructibility of the pulled-back direct image on a strictly totally disconnected base
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field, Y_I a quasi-compact quasi-separated adic space of topologically finite type over Spa(C, O_C), f_I: B_{Y_I} → Y_I the relative closed unit ball, n invertible in O_C and F_I a Huber-constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on B_{Y_I}. Let g: Y → Y_I be a morphism of adic spaces from a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space Y. Then for every q ≥ 0 the sheaf g^*R^q f_{I!}F_I on Y_ét = |Y| admits a finite partition of |Y| into constructible locally closed subsets on each of which it is constant with value a finitely generated ℤ/n-module; that is, it is constructible in the sense of ECD Definition 20.1 (i). This is the classical input of condition (ii) in ECD's proof of Theorem 24.1. There Y is strictly totally disconnected of characteristic p; it maps to Spa(K, O_K) for K the completion of F_p((ϖ^{1/p^∞})) and, having no nonsplit finite étale covers, to Spa(C, O_C) for C the completed algebraic closure of K. The approximation Y ~ lim_I Y_I of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids over the geometric pair (C, O_C) therefore has bases of topologically finite type over an algebraically closed field, and the form of Hub96 6.2.2 over a non-closed base field, which the wording of ECD's proof uses with K, is not needed. The statement concerns the pulled-back sheaf only; its identification with a direct image over Y is perfectoid-support-image-comparison.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete; Y_I quasi-compact quasi-separated of topologically finite type over Spa(C, O_C); F_I Huber-constructible; n invertible in O_C.
Y strictly totally disconnected perfectoid (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected), so that étale sheaves on Y are sheaves on |Y|.
In the application F_I is a descent of a constructible sheaf on the ball over Y to a finite stage; that descent (ECD Proposition 20.7 in the source) is requested from H0.
proofSteps: By smooth-family-constructibility over C, G := R^q f_{I!}F_I is Huber-constructible: there is a finite partition of |Y_I| into constructible locally closed subsets S_k such that the restriction of G to the pseudo-adic site (Y_I, S_k)_ét is locally constant of finite type.

g is spectral, so the g⁻¹(S_k) form a finite partition of |Y| into constructible locally closed subsets, and g^*G is locally constant of finite type on each g⁻¹(S_k) for the induced pseudo-adic topology.

Y is strictly totally disconnected: every étale cover of a quasi-compact open splits, so that topology is the topology of the spectral space g⁻¹(S_k). Finitely many quasi-compact opens of g⁻¹(S_k) trivialise g^*G; their Boolean combinations are constructible locally closed subsets of |Y| on which g^*G is constant with finitely generated value.

Application to ECD 24.1 (ii): Y → Spa(C, O_C) as in the statement; Y ~ lim_I Y_I with Y_I = Spa(S_I, S_I°) of topologically finite type over C (H2 approximation, the case C⁺ = O_C); a constructible sheaf on the ball over Y descends to some B_{Y_I} by the requested H0 coefficient descent.

A strictly totally disconnected X lives over an algebraically closed C, so the approximating bases can be taken over C.

nodes.title: Proper-support direct image of the relative ball over a perfectoid base: the base-change contract
nodes.statement: In the situation of perfectoid-base-constructibility-transfer, let Y ~ lim_J Y_J be the approximation of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids over (C, O_C), g_J: Y → Y_J its maps, B_Y the relative closed unit ball over Y and h_J: B_Y → B_{Y_J} the induced maps. Write f_J = f̄_J ∘ j_J with j_J a quasi-compact open immersion and f̄_J proper (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactification-proper-factorisation), and define the proper-support direct image over the non-noetherian base by R f_! := R f̄_* ∘ j_! for the base change f̄, j of this factorisation to Y. Contract: for every J, every constructible F_J on B_{Y_J} and every q ≥ 0 the base-change map g_J^*R^q f_{J!}F_J → R^q f_!(h_J^*F_J) is an isomorphism, and R f_! does not depend on J or on the factorisation. This is not covered by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/lower-shriek-base-change, which is stated for locally noetherian analytic bases, and it is requested from H3. ECD's proof of Theorem 24.1 obtains the identity R^j f_{X!}F = g^*R^j f_{X_i!}F_i from base change for diamonds, which belongs to DiamondSixOperations and cannot be used to prove the classical contract; the diamond proof itself needs only perfectoid-base-constructibility-transfer.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of perfectoid-base-constructibility-transfer, with the approximation Y ~ lim_J Y_J over (C, O_C).
The statement is a contract resting on the request to H3; it is not proof-closed.
proofSteps: Reduce to a quasi-compact quasi-separated direct image: R f_{J!} = R f̄_{J*} ∘ j_{J!}, and extension by zero commutes with pullback (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero).

The base change of f̄_J along the colimit-presented tilde-limit Y ~ lim Y_J is again a tilde-limit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change); the stalks of R^q f̄_* at a geometric point of Y are the cohomology of the fibre over the strict localisation (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation) and are the colimit of the finite-level groups by tilde-limit continuity (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity).

The stalk formula and continuity are needed here for a perfectoid, non-noetherian base and for the pseudo-adic complement of the ball in its compactification; these cases and the independence of the factorisation are the content of the request to H3.

nodes.title: Invariance of radial cohomology under surjective extensions of geometric field pairs
nodes.statement: Let ι: (C, C⁺) → (C′, C′⁺) be a surjective extension of geometric field pairs, that is ι⁻¹(C′⁺) = C⁺, let p be the residue characteristic exponent, n prime to p and M a ℤ/n-module. Let Y be a closed disc or a closed annulus over S = Spa(C, C⁺) with radius representatives in C^×, j: U → Y a quasi-compact open, and Y′, U′ their base changes to S′ = Spa(C′, C′⁺); Y′ is the disc or annulus with the same radius representatives over S′. Then pullback H^i(Y, j_!M) → H^i(Y′, j′_!M) is bijective for every i. This is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type applied to radial affinoids, the classical form of ECD Theorem 19.5 (iii) for them. The inclusion of the generic point Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, C⁺) is induced by the identity of C, which is not a surjective extension when C⁺ ≠ O_C; the comparison with the maximal plus ring is annulus-geometric-plus-ring.
hypotheses: C, C′ algebraically closed complete; ι surjective, i.e. ι⁻¹(C′⁺) = C⁺ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions); no hypothesis on the ranks of the plus rings.
n prime to the residue characteristic exponent; M any ℤ/n-module.

Apply ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type to (R, R⁺) and the quasi-compact open U.

nodes.title: Disc and annulus cohomology over a geometric point with an arbitrary plus ring
nodes.statement: Let C be algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean with residue characteristic exponent p, C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of any rank, S = Spa(C, C⁺) with generic point η = Spa(C, O_C), n prime to p and Λ = ℤ/n. Let A be a closed annulus over S with radius representatives in C^×, and A_η its fibre over η, the closed annulus over Spa(C, O_C). Then restriction H^q(A, Λ) → H^q(A_η, Λ) is an isomorphism for all q, so H⁰(A, Λ) = Λ, H¹(A, Λ) = Λ(−1) (generated over μ_n by the Kummer class of the coordinate) and H^q(A, Λ) = 0 for q ≥ 2. Likewise a closed disc over S has cohomology Λ in degree 0 only. This is the form in which ECD's proof of Theorem 19.5 (ii) uses the annulus: its base is an arbitrary geometric point Spa(C′, C′⁺) of a strictly totally disconnected space (the printed 'annulus over Spa(C, C⁺)' is the registered misprint PAPER-SCHOLZE-17/E55). No statement is made about proper-support cohomology over C⁺ ≠ O_C, which belongs to H3's recorded gap on traces and duality over higher-rank points.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete; C⁺ of any rank; n prime to the residue characteristic exponent.
Ordinary cohomology only.
proofSteps: A is a quasi-compact smooth adic curve over S (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/smooth-adic-curve) and Λ is locally constant, hence overconvergent; the last clause of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-cohomology-finiteness gives H^q(A, Λ) ≅ H^q(A_η, Λ), because A_η ⊆ A is the pro-open subspace of points lying over η and contains every rank-one point.
A_η is the closed annulus over Spa(C, O_C): apply annulus-cohomology; for the disc apply disc-cohomology.
The Kummer class is compatible with restriction to A_η by naturality of the Kummer sequence.

nodes.title: Proper algebraic/analytic direct-image comparison
nodes.statement: (Huber 3.7.1) Let R be an adic space, S a scheme and φ: R → S a morphism of locally ringed spaces; let X, Y be schemes locally of finite type over S and f: X → Y an S-morphism; put X^ad = X ×_S R, Y^ad = Y ×_S R (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification) with f^ad: X^ad → Y^ad, and let φ_X, φ_Y be the induced morphisms of étale sites, which form a commutative square with f and f^ad. (Theorem 3.7.2) If f is proper and Λ is a torsion ring, the base-change transformation φ_Y^* ∘ R⁺f_* → R⁺f^ad_* ∘ φ_X^* of functors D⁺(X_ét, Λ) → D⁺((Y^ad)_ét, Λ) is an isomorphism. Here φ^* is inverse image. No constructibility and no condition on the torsion relative to the residue characteristics is imposed. (Lemma 3.7.3) For proper f the morphism f^ad is separated and quasi-compact, indeed proper; this is imported from AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper (ii′). The generality of R is that in which the fibre product exists (R1); no non-noetherian extension is added.
hypotheses: f proper; Λ a torsion ring; X, Y locally of finite type over S; R an adic space for which the fibre products exist (Huber's standing condition).
The written proof of Lemma 3.7.3 uses that O_R(R) is noetherian in the non-discrete case (Chow's lemma); the general case is delegated in the book to a source that is not public.
Book proof inherited from the reviewed decomposition; not re-read.
proofSteps: Reduce to Y = S affine and R affinoid, and by proper base change for schemes along Spec O_R(R) → S (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2) to S = Spec O_R(R).

For a geometric point ξ of R with image η in S, the strict localisation R(ξ) is Spa(B, B⁺) with B the strict henselisation of O_R(R) at the support of η, not the original ring (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit).

f^ad is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-separated-proper), so (R^n f^ad_* φ_X^*F)_ξ = H^n(X^ad ×_R Spa(B, B⁺), G) by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation, while (R^n f_*F)_η = H^n(X ×_S Spec B, L).

B⁺ is henselian along its ideal of definition and X^ad ×_R Spa(B, B⁺) = (X ×_S Spec B) ×_{Spec B} Spa(B, B⁺); the relative comparison theorem 3.2.10 for the proper map X ×_S Spec B → Spec B (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12) identifies the two groups.

nodes.statement: For a commutative triangle of k-schemes U→^j X→^g Y with g proper, h=g∘j:U→Y an open immersion, j an open immersion and j(U)=g⁻¹(h(U)), every abelian sheaf F on U^rig_ét has a canonical isomorphism h^rig_!F→Rg^rig_* j^rig_!F. nodes.title: Finite-type algebraic/analytic comparison
nodes.statement: Let k be a complete nonarchimedean field, X, Y schemes locally of finite type over k, f: X → Y a k-morphism of finite type, X^rig, Y^rig the associated rigid varieties with f^rig, and φ_X, φ_Y the morphisms of étale sites. Let n ≥ 1 be prime to char(k) if char(k) > 0. Then for every constructible ℤ/n-module F on X_ét and every q ≥ 0 the base-change map φ_Y^* R^q f_*F → R^q f^rig_* φ_X^*F is bijective (Huber, Theorem 3.8.1). No properness is assumed. In characteristic zero the residue characteristic may divide n, which smooth analytic duality does not allow. In characteristic p the hypothesis is ℓ-torsion prime to p, and the proof route (Berkovich §7.5) uses relative Poincaré duality for smooth morphisms of pure dimension d for every d ≥ 0, not only for curves; this is the case ECD Proposition 27.2 uses, for affine space of every finite dimension over the completed algebraic closure of F_p((t)).
hypotheses: f of finite type; F constructible; n prime to char(k) when char(k) > 0. No condition on the residue characteristic in the statement.
Characteristic p: closed only when the requested H3 suffix (Hub96 5.7.2 and 7.5.3 in every dimension) is supplied. Characteristic zero: the reduction through purity 3.9.1(b) is a recorded gap.
proofSteps: Characteristic p, reduction (Berkovich, proof of Theorem 7.5.1 with base Spec k): by Deligne's generic base change and constructibility theorem and noetherian induction on Y it suffices to treat a dense open of Y; one reduces to f an open immersion with dense image, then by induction on the fibre dimension, projections to affine lines and a finite radicial base change to the case of Lemma 7.5.2: f smooth of pure dimension d and F locally constant, with all R^q f_!(F^∨) locally constant after shrinking Y. The scheme-side inputs are requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.

Characteristic p, duality step: Theorem 7.4.9 and its analogue for schemes (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:trace-purity) give R^q f_*F ≅ (R^{2d−q} f_!(F^∨))^∨(−d) on both sides, compatibly with analytification. The analytic statement, for every d, is Hub96 7.5.3 and is requested from H3 (the suffix H3:smooth-duality of RT-AREA-etale/5).
Characteristic p, compact supports: (R^q f_!G)^an ≅ R^q f^an_!G^an for compactifiable f and torsion G (Berkovich 7.1.4; Hub96 5.7.2, in the same request to H3).

Transport between Berkovich and adic étale topoi is only available for taut spaces, partially proper morphisms and overconvergent sheaves (Zavyalov A.15, A.18, A.19); analytified constructible sheaves are overconvergent.

Characteristic zero: Huber's route follows SGA 4 XVI §4 with proper-comparison-3-7-2, the purity theorem 3.9.1(b) and proper-open-excision; it is recorded as a gap. ECD uses Theorem 3.8.1 only in characteristic p (Proposition 27.2).

nodes.title: Stabilization of actual radius restriction maps
nodes.statement: With C=completed algebraic closure of F_p((t)), ℓ≠p, m finite and constructible coefficients descended from F_p affine space, the restriction RΓ(B_n,A)→RΓ(B_1,A) is an equivalence for some n>1 in ℤ[1/p] sufficiently close to 1 and for the cofinal geometric sequence of radii n^j obtained by scaling. The proof requires both finite total cohomology and overconvergent neighborhood continuity: colim_{n>1,n→1} H^q(B_n,A)≅H^q(B_1,A). Automorphisms over F_p sending t to t^n yield equal finite dimensions, but they alone do not prove that the restriction maps are isomorphisms. Uniform surjectivity in the finitely many degrees, followed by equal finite cardinality, does.

Positive rational p-power indices and their chosen roots; overconvergence of the analytified sheaf; finite total Fℓ cohomology.

By finite-polydisc-cohomology only finitely many degrees occur and each group is finite, so one n > 1 in ℤ[1/p] makes H^q(B_n) → H^q(B_1) surjective in all degrees.

nodes.statement: Let X → S be a flat morphism of admissible formal schemes over a complete discrete valuation ring whose associated rigid morphism is a smooth rigid curve fibration, and let U be the image of X in S. X is S-compactifiable if there is an open S-immersion of X into a flat projective formal curve C → U whose associated rigid curve C_rig → U_rig is smooth (Lütkebohmert, Definition 5.6). The curve C is projective over the image U, not over S. For an open formal subscheme U′ ⊆ S, X is S-compactifiable over U′ if X ×_S U′ is U′-compactifiable.

On generic fibres an S-compactification gives an open immersion of X_rig into a smooth proper curve over U_rig, a compactification in the sense of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactifiable-morphism.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal compactification of relative curves
nodes.statement: (Proposition 5.4.) Over a complete discrete valuation ring, let f: X → S be a flat affine morphism of admissible formal schemes with reduced geometric fibres that are equidimensional of dimension 1. Then there are a stratification S₀ = S₀¹ ∪ … ∪ S₀^r of the special fibre by subschemes and a rig-étale cover S′ → S such that X′ = X ×_S S′ admits a projective compactification P^ρ over the formal completion of S′ along each stratum, which can be chosen smooth at infinity, together with a closed subscheme Δ^ρ of P^ρ that is an ample relative Cartier divisor. (Lemma 5.5.) Around a point s of S₀, with 𝒥 a finitely generated ideal with zero set the closure of s: there are an open neighbourhood U of s, a rig-étale cover U′ → U and, for every n, a projective flat scheme P′(n) over the reduction U′(n) modulo 𝒥ⁿ with an open immersion of X′(n), such that the geometric fibres of P′(n) are reduced, P′(n) is smooth along P′(n) − X′(n), X′(n) is fibrewise dense, and there is an ample invertible sheaf O(Δ(n)) for a relative Cartier divisor Δ(n) containing P′(n) − X′(n) and contained in the smooth locus; the P′(n) and Δ(n) can be chosen coherently in n. These are compactifications over completions along strata of the special fibre, a topology finer than the given one; they are not yet a compactification over the rigid generic fibre.
hypotheses: R a complete discrete valuation ring (standing notation, p. 167); X → S flat affine, admissible formal schemes; geometric fibres reduced and equidimensional of dimension 1.
Rig-étale covers and formal completions along subschemes of the special fibre are requested from AdicSpacesPartII R2.
proofSteps: Lemma 5.5: over the residue field of s take the projective closure of the fibre curve; after a finite radicial extension of the residue field it is smooth at infinity with boundary points étale over the field, and carries an ample Cartier divisor containing the boundary. The projective model of a curve over a field is Tau Ceti's (AlgebraicCurves, Layer 12).

Realise the radicial extension by a rig-étale cover (blow up the ideal (p, 𝒥) and adjoin p-th roots on the two charts), then lift the smooth affine neighbourhood of infinity, the gluing map and the Cartier divisor through the nilpotent thickenings modulo 𝒥ⁿ; ampleness of the divisor gives projectivity at every level.
Proposition 5.4 follows by noetherian induction on S₀; in residue characteristic zero no base change is needed.

sources.match: Hypotheses; the conclusion gives a stratification of S₀, a rig-étale cover S′ → S, projective compactifications P^ρ over the completions along the strata, smooth at infinity, and an ample relative Cartier divisor Δ^ρ on P^ρ.
The divisor contains the boundary and lies in the smooth locus: this is in Lemma 5.5, at every level n, not in the statement of Proposition 5.4.

nodes.title: Extension of curve compactifications by approximation
nodes.statement: (Proposition 5.7.) Let K be the fraction field of a complete discrete valuation ring R, and X → S a flat affine morphism of admissible formal schemes whose associated rigid map is a smooth rigid curve fibration. Let V = Spf(B) be an open affine formal subscheme of X that is faithfully flat over an open affine U = Spf(A) of S, and assume V is S-compactifiable. Then, after base change by an admissible formal blowing-up S′ → S, there are an admissible formal blowing-up X′ → X and an open formal subscheme V′ of X′ such that the schematic closure of (X′ ×_X V)₀ is contained in V′₀ and V′ is S-compactifiable. (Lemma 5.8.) The Hilbert scheme H(d, g, N) of closed subschemes of P^N that are smooth curves of genus g and degree d is smooth over ℤ if d ≥ 2g − 1.
hypotheses: Exactly the hypotheses of Proposition 5.7: complete discrete valuation ring, X → S flat affine with smooth rigid curve fibration, V affine and faithfully flat over an affine open U of S, V S-compactifiable.

The approximation theorem 7.4 and Proposition 7.5 of the same paper are used with their hypotheses (Weierstrass domain, relatively S-compact image, rig-smooth target) and are requested from AdicSpacesPartII R2.
proofSteps: Embed the compactification C of V in P^N_U by a very ample line bundle of fibre degree d ≥ 2g − 1; by formal GAGA it is algebraic, and it is classified by a map from U to the Hilbert scheme whose rigid part lands in the open H(d, g, N) of smooth curves, which is smooth by Lemma 5.8 (lifting of curves and of relative Cartier divisors, and H¹(C, O_C(Δ)) = 0 by Serre duality, from Tau Ceti's JacobianChallenge Layer B).

Since the image is relatively compact, Theorem 7.4 (with Proposition 7.5, Elkik's lemma) gives, after an admissible blowing-up of S, an open U′ whose special fibre contains the closure of that of U and a map to the Hilbert scheme agreeing with the given one to a prescribed level; pull back the universal curve.

Apply 7.5 and 7.4 again to extend the open immersion V → C to an open V′ of a blowing-up X′ whose special fibre contains the closure of that of V, keeping an open immersion on generic fibres; a further admissible blowing-up makes it an open immersion and the model flat (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/flattening-by-blow-up).

nodes.title: Compactification of smooth rigid curves over an algebraically closed field
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field and X a quasi-compact separated smooth rigid curve over C. (L) Local form: every point of X has a quasi-compact open neighbourhood V with an open immersion V → X′ into a proper smooth rigid curve over C. (G) Global form, as ECD's proof of Theorem 25.1 writes it: X itself admits an open immersion into a proper smooth rigid curve. Lütkebohmert's Theorem 5.3 gives (L) over a discretely valued field (with S a point, 'étale locally on S' is a finite extension of the field). An algebraically closed C is not discretely valued, and Remark 6.7 of the same paper says that discreteness is assumed throughout and only asserts that the results extend to arbitrary height-one valuations if parts of EGA are rewritten for universally coherent base rings. So (L) over C is a recorded gap, and (G) needs in addition a globalisation that Theorem 5.3 does not state. The consumer needs only (L): the cone in the biduality reduction is a direct sum of contributions at finitely many frontier points, each of which can be computed in a neighbourhood (curve-boundary-direct-summand).

nodes.title: Finite frontier support contributions
nodes.statement: Let C be algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean, X a quasi-compact separated smooth rigid curve over Spa(C, O_C), j: U → X a quasi-compact open and ℓ a prime invertible in O_C. The frontier B = Ū∖U of U in the adic space X is a finite discrete set of points (requested from AdicEtaleGeometry A2; for an annulus in the disc it consists of the two rank-two points of Ito's Example A.1). For M ∈ D(F_ℓ), let α_X: j_!M → RHom(Rj_*F_ℓ, M) be the map adjoint to j_!M ⊗ Rj_*F_ℓ = j_!(M ⊗ j^*Rj_*F_ℓ) = j_!M → M. Then α_X is an isomorphism over U and over the complement of Ū, its cone is supported on B, and RΓ(X, cone(α_X)) is the direct sum over b ∈ B of contributions that depend only on an open neighbourhood of b in X. The diamond biduality theorem itself is DiamondSixOperations S6.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete with plus ring O_C; X quasi-compact separated smooth of pure dimension one; j quasi-compact open; ℓ invertible in O_C.
No compactification of X is used in this statement.
proofSteps: Over U both sides are M and α_X is the identity; over the open complement of Ū both sides vanish. Hence the cone is supported on the closed set B.

B is finite and discrete (requested from AdicEtaleGeometry A2), so a complex supported on B is the direct sum of its restrictions to the points of B (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/localisation-sequence), and each summand is determined by the restriction of α_X to a neighbourhood of the point.
Internal Hom and the unbounded derived category are EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1's.

nodes.title: Proper-curve local duality reduction
nodes.statement: Let X′ be a proper smooth rigid curve over Spa(C, O_C), f its structure map, j: U → X′ a quasi-compact open, ℓ invertible in O_C, and N ∈ D(F_ℓ) with M = N(1)[2] = f^!N in the normalisation of H3. Then RHom(Rj_*F_ℓ, M) = RHom_{D(F_ℓ)}(RΓ(U, F_ℓ), N) and RΓ(X′, j_!M) = RΓ_c(U, N(1)[2]), and the map between them induced by α_{X′} is the map given by the Poincaré duality pairing RΓ_c(U, F_ℓ(1))[2] ⊗ RΓ(U, F_ℓ) → F_ℓ of H3; it is an isomorphism. Hence α_{X′} induces an isomorphism on global sections for every M, and with curve-boundary-direct-summand and the local form of the compactification export, α_X induces an isomorphism on global sections for every quasi-compact separated smooth rigid curve X over C and quasi-compact open U. This applies H3's curve duality; it does not plan a second duality theorem.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete, plus ring O_C; ℓ invertible in O_C; X′ proper smooth of pure dimension one; U quasi-compact open.
The conclusion for a general X is conditional on the local compactification over C (the recorded gap).
Arbitrary N ∈ D(F_ℓ) is reached from N = F_ℓ because RΓ(U, F_ℓ) and RΓ_c(U, F_ℓ) are finite, so both sides commute with colimits in N.
proofSteps: On the proper curve X′ proper support equals global sections, so RΓ(X′, j_!M) = RΓ_c(U, M); by the adjunction between Rf_! = Rf_* and f^!, RHom(Rj_*F_ℓ, f^!N) = RHom(Rf_*Rj_*F_ℓ, N) = RHom(RΓ(U, F_ℓ), N).
RΓ(U, F_ℓ) and RΓ_c(U, F_ℓ) are finite (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-cohomology-finiteness), so both sides commute with all colimits in N and it suffices to take N = F_ℓ.

For N = F_ℓ, check that the map induced by α_{X′} is the one given by the cup product and the trace of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-trace; then ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-duality-perfect-pairing shows it is an isomorphism. ECD leaves this compatibility to the reader (registered as PAPER-SCHOLZE-17/E72), so it is a step of this node and not an assumption.
Conclude for X by curve-boundary-direct-summand, one frontier point at a time, with the neighbourhoods of the compactification export.

The direct-summand statement; only the contributions at frontier points lying in X are compared.

nodes.title: The compactification direct summand
nodes.statement: In the situation of curve-boundary-contributions, let V ⊆ X be a quasi-compact open and i: V → X′ an open immersion into a proper smooth rigid curve over C. Write U_V = U ∩ V, j′: U_V → X′ and α_{X′}: j′_!M → RHom(Rj′_*F_ℓ, M). Then i^*cone(α_{X′}) = cone(α_X)|_V, the frontier of U_V in X′ is finite and discrete, and for every frontier point b of U in X that lies in V, with V a neighbourhood of b on which U_V = U ∩ V, the contribution of b to RΓ(X, cone(α_X)) is a direct summand of RΓ(X′, cone(α_{X′})), by an explicit inclusion and projection. Consequently, if every frontier point of U has such a neighbourhood (the local form (L) of the compactification export) and α_{X′} is an isomorphism for every proper smooth curve X′ and quasi-compact open, then α_X is an isomorphism. For V = X this is the statement in ECD's proof of Theorem 25.1.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of curve-boundary-contributions.
For each frontier point, a quasi-compact open neighbourhood with an open immersion into a proper smooth rigid curve; a single embedding of X is not required.
The frontier is the topological frontier in the adic space; its points are of rank two, not classical boundary points.
proofSteps: Restriction to an open is exact and commutes with j_!, Rj_* and internal Hom, so α_{X′} restricts on V to the map α for U_V ⊆ V, which agrees with α_X near every frontier point of U lying in V.

The frontier of U_V in X′ is finite and discrete (curve-boundary-contributions applied to X′), so RΓ(X′, cone(α_{X′})) is the direct sum of the contributions of its points; those of the frontier points of U in V are among them, and by locality they are the contributions computed in X.
Inclusion of and projection onto these summands compose to the identity.

For the approximation Y ~ lim Y_J of a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space over Spa(C, O_C) (H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids), with R f_! over Y defined through the base change of a finite-level factorisation f_J = f̄_J ∘ j_J: independence of J and of the factorisation, and the base-change isomorphism g_J^*R^q f_{J!}F_J ≅ R^q f_!(h_J^*F_J) for constructible F_J. gaps.detail: ECD's proof of Theorem 25.1 embeds a quasi-compact smooth curve over an algebraically closed C into a proper smooth curve by [Lüt95, Theorem 5.3]. Closing it means either running Lütkebohmert's §5 and §7 over the non-noetherian ring of integers of C (see the request to AdicSpacesPartII R2) or citing a theorem that covers this case. sourceIssues.printed: The source cites [Lüt95, Theorem 5.3] to embed X in a rigid-analytic curve X′ that is proper and smooth.
sourceIssues.correction: The cited theorem is over the fraction field of a complete discrete valuation ring and gives a compactification étale-locally on the base and locally on the curve. For the algebraically closed C of the proof one needs its extension to nondiscretely valued fields, which Remark 6.7 of Lütkebohmert's paper asserts without proof. A global embedding is not needed: the cone is a direct sum of contributions at the finitely many frontier points, so it suffices to embed a neighbourhood of each frontier point into a proper smooth curve, which is what the theorem provides once it is available over C. Footnote 7 of ECD names [GW21] for a different treatment of this case.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 5.3 reads: 'Let K be the field of fractions of a complete discrete valuation ring R. Let f_K : X_K → S_K be a smooth rigid curve fibration. Then, étale locally on S_K and locally on X_K, there exists a smooth projective S_K-compactification.' Remark 6.7 reads: 'Throughout the paper we always assumed that the valuation of the base field is discrete.' An algebraically closed nontrivially valued field has a divisible value group and is not discretely valued, and a compactification of open pieces of X is not an embedding of X. So the cited theorem does not justify the sentence as written. The statement of Theorem 25.1 is not put in doubt.
